accepted.sentence: Typically forged from hardened steel, its long handle transmits torque from the user's hand to a fastener.
Open-ended designs have two flat jaws separated by a gap that fits around opposing sides of a hexagonal fastener.
Some heads encircle a fastener with an internally shaped ring, distributing contact across multiple flats.
Adjustable models use a sliding jaw moved by a knurled worm screw along the head.
Many models have a polished or chrome-plated surface that resists corrosion and makes oil easier to wipe away.
A handle may have a slight offset near its head, creating clearance from nearby surfaces.
Ratcheting heads contain a reversible pawl mechanism, allowing rotation in one direction without lifting from the fastener.
Some have differently sized ends, combining an open jaw at one end with a closed ring at the other.
